directAnswer: To update a relational database, use SQL commands such as UPDATE to modify existing records in a specified table.
summary: Updating a relational database involves executing SQL commands to change data while ensuring data integrity.

sections.heading: Understanding SQL UPDATE
sections.body: The SQL UPDATE statement allows you to modify existing records in a table. You can specify which records to update using a WHERE clause to avoid altering all records.

sections.heading: Platform-Specific Steps
sections.body: Steps may vary based on the database management system (DBMS) you are using.

steps.title: Connect to the Database
steps.detail: Use your preferred database client or command line to connect to the database.

steps.title: Write the UPDATE Statement
steps.detail: Construct your SQL UPDATE statement. Example: `UPDATE table_name SET column1 = value1 WHERE condition;`

steps.title: Execute the Query
steps.detail: Run the SQL command through your database client or command line interface.

steps.title: Verify Changes
steps.detail: Use a SELECT statement to verify that the changes have been applied correctly.

faqs.question: What happens if I forget the WHERE clause?
faqs.answer: If you omit the WHERE clause, all records in the table will be updated, which can lead to data loss.

faqs.question: Can I update multiple columns at once?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can update multiple columns in a single UPDATE statement by separating each column assignment with a comma.

faqs.question: Is it possible to roll back an update?
faqs.answer: If your database supports transactions, you can roll back an update if it has not been committed.

caveats: Ensure you have proper backups before performing updates.
Be cautious with the WHERE clause to avoid unintended data changes.
